findings.claim: After a crop, a resize (an upscale's landing included) or an extend, a Deep paint layer's pixels are replaced at the new size and marked dirty, but nothing schedules their upload. The autosave written 1.5 s later names the new document size together with the layer's old-size file. A crash or kill before the next pixel edit, save or clean quit therefore restores the layer with its paint dropped (tiles, file of 32 MP or more) or silently stretched into the new size (smaller files, canvas backend).
findings.scenario: Tiles backend, 15000 x 10000 document, Deep paint layer with paint, its file already uploaded (ref R0, 15000 x 10000). Steps: (1) Canvas tool, crop 2000 px off the left. cropCanvasNow sets l.px = l.px.resized(nw, nh, ...) and l.dirty = true, then calls notifyChanged(), which only starts host.changed's 1.5 s saveAll. Neither scheduleAutosave() nor syncLayers() is called; they are reached only from markLayerChanged / markMaskChanged, a turn or straighten, a document save, a local run, or a clean quit. (2) The user goes on without a pixel edit (filter sliders, prompt, an API run) and the renderer dies (the OOM cases in docs/BUGS.md, a kill, power loss). (3) At the next start autosave.json has width 13000 and the layer's ref R0. setValue streams R0 at 15000 x 10000 and throws at the size check, so the layer comes back empty with only a '(its paint)' note: all paint on the layer is gone, not the last 15 s. With a file under 32 MP, or on the canvas backend, Layer.fromImage(limg, this.width, this.height) scales the old file into the new size, so after a crop the paint is squashed and misplaced with no notice. Ordinary pixel layers are safe in the same crash because crop only shifts x/y and their file stays valid. Turn and straighten avoid this by calling syncLayers() at once. Filter-layer masks have the same hole since before this diff (maskDirty set, never scheduled; the restore stretches them).

findings.claim: A held stack program is documented as 'the picture of this moment': every pixel layer and every filter mask is held as a copy-on-write clone. A Deep paint step holds only the live layer object, and each band reads `layer.px` when it is filtered. A change to the Deep paint layer between the hold and the band reads (a committed stroke, Fill, an undo that replaces px, a live re-wrap) therefore reaches the run's crop, in whole or only in the later bands. readBoxBytes has no compositeVersion check, unlike encodeComposite.
findings.scenario: Tiles backend, large picture, Deep paint layer shown, selection made. Click Generate: prepareCropAsync calls editor.holdRunStack() (clones taken now), then awaits the stitch worker's 'plan', then regionBytes -> readBoxBytes(held) -> fillBoxFromStack reads the box band by band (programRows, up to 2,048 rows each, each band awaiting the pool). If a brush stroke on the Deep paint layer is released, or Ctrl+Z replaces its px, during that window, bands filtered afterwards composite the new paint while earlier bands and every ordinary layer show the click's state. The crop sent to the model (a paid API run included) is a mix of two states. The window is short (hundreds of ms to a couple of seconds at 15k), so this is a narrow race.

The promise at inpaint_ed_stack.js:741-743: 'copy-on-write clones taken before this returns its promise, so the picture is the one of this moment whatever the window does while the crop is planned'. stitch.js:858-866: `holding = editor.holdRunStack({ forRun: true }); ... await stitchCall("plan", ...); held = holding ? await holding : null; ... await regionBytes(editor, p.x0, p.y0, p.cw, p.ch, holding ? held : undefined);`. readBoxBytes (inpaint_ed_stack.js:757-782) checks no version; encodeComposite does (inpaint_ed_composite.js:649, 656).

Alternatively re-check compositeVersion in readBoxBytes for programs that hold such a step and re-read once.

findings.claim: A Deep paint layer's alpha lock is honoured by the brush, the live stroke and the bucket and is written by getValue, but the filter-layer branch of setValue does not read it back. After a restart, a .scumble open or a tab restore the lock is off and paint lands on transparent areas again.

Strokes now use source-atop (ownPixelsFor :787, commit in inpaint_ed_strokes.js, bucket inpaint_ed_shape.js:349). Save the document or quit and reopen: the layer is rebuilt without alphaLock, and the next stroke or agent fill paints outside the existing paint.

findings.claim: The "Generate the new border" layers step is pushed before Generate starts and is never taken off when the run lands nothing (a refusal after the pre-checks, a failed or cancelled run). The undo stack then holds a step that changes nothing on top of the extend, while extend_canvas's description and its error text tell the caller that Ctrl+Z / undo takes the extend back.
findings.scenario: MCP: extend_canvas {right: 512, generate: true} with a local recipe while ComfyUI is not connected (or an API recipe with a missing key, an empty prompt on a promptRequired recipe, a provider error, a cancel_run). The pre-checks pass (wired, no providerPending), the canvas is extended (every visible layer baked into the base), pushUndo records the layers step, generate.run throws. The agent reads "The canvas was extended ... (its own undo step); the generate ... failed" and the description "the extend stays, Ctrl+Z takes it back", calls undo once: stepped is 1, but only the empty layers step went; the canvas is still extended and baked. A retry of extend_canvas then extends a second time. In the UI the same: after a failed run of Generate the new border the first Ctrl+Z does nothing visible.
findings.evidence: renderer/commands_edit.js:305 `ed.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Generate the new border" });` 306 `try { generated = await RunCommandsPart.generate.run(ed, { timeout: a.timeout }); }` 307-310 the catch only rethrows (`The canvas was extended to ... (its own undo step); the generate of the new border failed`), no pop of the step. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1309-1311 `const refused = this._eachArea || !s.wired || (this.providerPending && ...); if (!refused) this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Generate the new border" }); this.lastExtendGenerate = this.generate();` - generate()'s later failures (inpaint_canvas.js:1319-1326 catch of host.queueGenerate) are not among `refused`. The undo command (commands_edit.js:218) answers only `{ undo, redo, stepped, status }`.
findings.fix: Remember the pushed snapshot and the history length; when generate ends with an error and nothing landed (ed.history.length unchanged, the step still on top of ed.undo and no run of the document left in providerPending / _localRuns), take the step off again (pop + releaseSnapshot + historyChanged). In the UI path do the same on the promise of this.generate(). Keep it for a timeout whose run may still land.
findings.why: Lines are as quoted. renderer/commands_edit.js:305 pushes a `layers` step unconditionally once the extend succeeded, 306-311 only rethrow; nothing pops it. The pre-checks at 277-282 cover only no growing side, _eachArea, providerPending and `wired`; generate.run (renderer/commands_runs.js:397-436) can still throw afterwards: `run.error` at 416 (missing key, empty prompt on a promptRequired recipe, a token refusal), `failed()` at 419/426 (ComfyUI not connected, provider error), "no result arrived" at 436, a cancel. pushUndo (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:445-472) always pushes a snapshot when an image is loaded (no dedupe of an unchanged state), and stepHistory (518-531) counts a step as done when the stack shrank, so `undo` returns stepped: 1 while only the no-op layers step went and the canvas stays extended and baked. The description at 271 says "the extend stays, Ctrl+Z takes it back" and the error says "(its own undo step)", so one undo is the natural reading; two are needed. UI path the same: inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1309-1311 skips the push only for the three immediate refusals, not for generate()'s later failures. Outcome is not data loss (a second undo takes the extend back, list_history shows the "Generate the new border" row), but an agent retrying after one undo extends twice. Not found in docs/BUGS.md or PLAN_0_1_57.md; the feature (item 63) is newer than the earlier reviews' verified.json files, so not known.

findings.claim: A local ComfyUI result is still loading its picture (addResults awaits loadImageEl) when execution_success (or status queue_remaining 0) has already removed the prompt from editor._localRuns. In that window turnBlocked() answers "", so a geometry step (the undo of the extend, a crop, a turn, extend_canvas) runs, and the result layer is then added at the x / y of the old geometry.
findings.scenario: Generate the new border with a recipe on the user's ComfyUI (a remote one makes the window a second or more: the result PNG comes through /comfy/view). The user wants it back and presses Ctrl+Z twice during the run: the first takes the layers step, the second is refused with "Press Ctrl+Z again when it is in". The progress ends (execution_success), the user presses Ctrl+Z again while the picture is still downloading: `_localRuns` is empty, the canvas step is applied, the document is back at its old size. Then addLayer puts "Result n" at r.x, r.y of the extended picture: a layer shifted by the extend's left / top, partly outside the picture, with no undo step of its own.

findings.claim: When the shadow grid passes the cell cap the coverage is averaged f x f, and the object's box and foot are then taken again at coverage >= 0.5. Parts thinner than about f/2 cells fall under 0.5: a thin object is refused with "has no opaque part in the picture: it casts no shadow", and an object standing on thin parts gets its foot (and so the whole shadow) at the lowest thick part instead of where it stands.
findings.scenario: A cut-out that is tall and very thin (a pole, a rod, a line 3 cells wide on the 2048-cell working grid, i.e. under about 0.15 % of its height) with contact_shadow {distance: 300, softness: 100}: shadowExtent wants 237,268,910 cells, f = 8, the coarse coverage is at most 3/8 everywhere, alphaBox answers null, shadowGrid returns grid null and the command throws "<layer> has no opaque part in the picture: it casts no shadow" for a fully opaque object (checked with a Node one-liner on the module: `NULL after 1 coarsenings, src 2 256`). With defaults (distance 30, softness 8) the same layer gets its shadow. In the dialog the preview (1 M cells) coarsens sooner (f 4-7 at distance 60-100 / softness 20-40) and simply disappears without a word.
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_shadow.js:111-116 `for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) { const e = shadowExtent(src.alpha, src.w, src.h, params); if (!e) return { grid: null, src }; if (e.cells <= maxCells || ...) break; src = coarserCoverage(src, Math.max(2, Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(e.cells / maxCells)))); }`; inpaint_shadow.js:108-110 `const box = alphaBox(alpha, w, h); if (!box) return null;` with 31 `const SOLID = 0.5;` and 64 `if (alpha[row + x] >= solid)`; 126 `sum[i] = n[i] ? sum[i] / n[i] : 0` (plain average). inpaint_ed_shadow.js:228 `if (!grid) { this.setStatus(`${layer.name} has no opaque part in the picture: it casts no shadow.`, "info"); return null; }`; contactShadow (inpaint_shadow.js:137) also recomputes the box from the coarse alpha.
findings.fix: Take the object's box (and foot) once on the uncoarsened coverage and carry it through the coarsening scaled by f (contactShadow already accepts `box`), and coarsen with a max instead of a mean for the solid test (or lower the solid threshold to 0.5 / f for coarsened sources); keep the averaged alpha for the shadow's strength.
findings.why:
The lines are as quoted at a808738b and no guard stops the path; not run in the app, checked by reading and by hand arithmetic.

**Path:** `addContactShadow` (inpaint_ed_shadow.js:218-228) calls `shadowSource(layer, SHADOW_WORK)` and then `shadowGrid(src0, p)`. The dialog's preview takes the same route with `SHADOW_MAX_CELLS_PREVIEW` (line 285).

**The loop (inpaint_ed_shadow.js:111-116):** each pass calls `shadowExtent` on the current source and returns `{ grid: null, src }` when it answers null. Otherwise it replaces the source with `coarserCoverage(src, f)`.

**Why the box vanishes (inpaint_shadow.js):**
- `shadowExtent` (108-110) takes `alphaBox` at `SOLID = 0.5` (line 31, test at line 64).
- `coarserCoverage` (119-128) is a plain f x f mean (line 126).
- So a part narrower than f/2 cells falls below 0.5 after one coarsening, and `alphaBox` answers null on the second pass.

**The scenario's numbers hold:** `shadowParams` allows distance up to 300 and softness up to 100 (lines 47-48), the same range the dialog fields offer (lines 300-301). For H = 2048:
- R = 6144, sigma = 2048, pad = 6146, up = 861.
- The grid is about 12.3k x 19.3k, roughly 237 M cells against the 4 M cap, so f = ceil(sqrt(59.3)) = 8.
- A 3-cell-wide column averages to at most 3/8, below 0.5.

**Outcome:** `addContactShadow` line 228 reports "has no opaque part in the picture: it casts no shadow" for a fully opaque thin object. In the preview, `shadowPreviewCanvas(used, null)` returns null (line 165), so the overlay disappears with no message.

**Second half of the claim also holds:** `contactShadow` (line 137) recomputes the box and foot from the coarse alpha, since `shadowGrid` passes no `box` (line 121). An object standing on thin legs therefore gets its foot at the lowest part that is still at least 0.5 after averaging.

**Not known:** `docs/BUGS.md` has no entry for contact shadow or coarsening. I did not open the three `verified.json` files or `PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`; they are dated 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-12, before this feature was built on 2026-11-15/16.

**Severity nice:** it needs a very thin object or thin supports together with extreme distance and softness. No data is lost; the message is misleading and the shadow is missing or misplaced. Lower settings work.

findings.claim: Since d6753999 an extend keeps hidden layers. A hidden layer that is clipped to a visible base keeps its `clip` flag while its base is baked into the new base and dropped, so it now clips to whatever unclipped kept layer happens to lie below it (another hidden layer, a control layer), or to nothing.
findings.scenario: Stack bottom to top: hidden paint layer X (a small sketch), visible cut-out B, hidden layer C clipped to B (an alternative texture). Extend the canvas (also through Generate the new border). B is baked and removed; kept = [X, C], C.clip still true. When the user shows C again it is clipped to X: it shows only inside X's small shape (or, with X hidden, not at all, since a clip to a hidden base draws nothing), though the status said "2 hidden layers stay layers, moved with the picture". The pixels are still there (releasing the clip brings them back), but the layer no longer looks as it did before the extend.

findings.fix: For a kept layer with `clip` whose clip target (clipTargetOf before the change) is not kept, set `l.clip = false` (its base is part of the picture now) and say so in the hidden-layers note; or keep it clipped only when its target is in keptSet.

findings.claim: The picker takes a frame without ever checking that the seek to the shown time succeeded: settled() resolves after its 10 s timeout whatever the element's state, frameFile() then draws whatever the <video> still holds and names it after v.currentTime, and nothing listens for the element's `error` once the picker is open. A video whose data ends before its stated length (a truncated or half-downloaded MP4 / MOV with the index at the front, a damaged stretch) therefore yields a picture of another moment (the last frame decoded) or an empty one, landed as a new picture / layer / reference with no error.
findings.scenario: State: an MP4 with moov at the start saying 60 s, the file cut at about 20 s (interrupted copy or download). Steps: File > Open (or drop) -> loadVideo succeeds (first frame decodes, duration finite, so findDuration is skipped) -> drag the slider to 40 s (range 'input' handler sets v.currentTime, line 198) -> the seek cannot complete (the read runs past the file; the element fires `error`, which only loadVideo's once-listener handled and that is long gone) -> click 'Open as new picture'. take() -> frameFile() -> settled(v) waits 10 s on seeked/loadeddata/canplay, then its timeout calls done() and resolves -> videoWidth/Height are still > 0 -> drawImage(v) paints the frame from before the seek (or nothing if the element dropped its frame) -> a PNG named '<stem> 40.000s.png' is opened as the picture; the status line reports success. Wrong pixels land silently; the user sees a frame that is not the one at the time shown. (Chromium's behaviour on the failed seek was not run here; the code-level fact is that neither the timeout path nor v.error / v.seeking / readyState is checked before the draw.)
findings.evidence: renderer/videoframe.js:113-123 `function settled(v) { ... if (!v.seeking && v.readyState >= 2) { resolve(); return; } const t = setTimeout(done, 10000); function done() { ...; resolve(); }` (the timeout resolves like a success). :126-139 `export async function frameFile(v, name) { await settled(v); const w = v.videoWidth, h = v.videoHeight; if (!(w > 0 && h > 0)) throw ...; c.getContext("2d").drawImage(v, 0, 0, w, h); ... return new File([blob], `${stem} ${v.currentTime.toFixed(3)}s.png`...` (no check of v.error, v.seeking or readyState). :62 the only `error` listener is `{ once: true }` inside loadVideo; showPicker (159-397) adds listeners for timeupdate / seeked / pause / play only (263-266).
findings.fix: Make settled() resolve with a boolean (false on its timeout) and let frameFile() throw when it is false, when v.error is set, when v.seeking is still true or readyState < 2 ('the video could not be read at this time'); take() already shows frameFile's error in the info line and re-enables the buttons. Add an `error` listener in showPicker that writes the MEDIA_ERRORS text into the info line.
findings.why:
The lines are as quoted at a808738b (renderer/videoframe.js), and no guard stops the path. Chromium's behaviour on the failed seek was not run (read-only, no app).

- **settled() 113-123:** the 10 s timeout calls `done()`, which resolves exactly like the success path; the caller cannot tell the two apart.
- **frameFile() 126-139:** after `await settled(v)` it checks only `videoWidth` / `videoHeight` > 0, which stay set after a media error. It never reads `v.error`, `v.seeking` or `readyState`, then draws the element and names the file after `v.currentTime`, the seek target.
- **take() 343-359:** it adds no check of its own; `finish()` returns `time: v.currentTime`.
- **Error listener:** the only one is the `{ once: true }` listener inside `loadVideo` (line 62). `showPicker` listens for timeupdate / seeked / pause / play only (263-266).
- **Entry:** the range `input` handler (198) sets `v.currentTime` unguarded, as do `seconds()`, `jump()` and the gate's `seek`.

So a seek that never completes (truncated or damaged file, or a read slower than 10 s) yields a PNG of the previously decoded frame, labelled with the target time, and no error is shown.

Severity is "nice" rather than "should": it needs a damaged or truncated file, and the picker's own `<video>` shows the same stale frame, so the picture taken is the one the user sees. What is wrong is the time in the file name and result, and the missing error line. Not known: docs/BUGS.md has no entry for videoframe or `settled`. I did not grep the three verified.json files or PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md; the reviews are dated 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-12, before item 68 was built (2026-11-15/16).

findings.claim: While a frame is being encoded the picker still accepts seeks (the slider, Shift+Arrow, Home / End), and the frame's file name and the returned `time` are read from v.currentTime after the PNG encode: the layer or picture is named after a time that is not the frame's.

Press Enter ('Open as new picture'), and within the PNG encode (toBlob of 3840 x 2160, tens to hundreds of ms) press End or Shift+Right, or nudge the slider. take() set busy and disabled the buttons, but seconds() (327-331), jump() (333-338) and the range's input handler (198) do not look at `busy`, and the slider is not in the disabled list. drawImage already ran with the 3.200 s frame; after `await toBlob` the name is built from the new v.currentTime, so the tab / layer is called e.g. 'clip 58.000s' and the result's `time` says 58 while the pixels are from 3.2 s.

findings.function: depthFromPoints (and computeDepthMap line 163, depth_from_layer line 521) -> mapToJSON
findings.claim: The new depth-from-points map stores its whole raw disparity Float32Array (points map size, 768 px long side, about 393,000 floats) in map.meta; mapToJSON serialises meta with JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(meta)), so every getValue() of the document carries the array as a {"0":..,"1":..} object: about 11 MB of JSON and about 170 ms per call, in the autosave bundle, the dirty hash and the .scumble state. The flaw predates the diff (Depth Anything's raw, about 200k floats, about 5-6 MB; 'finest' detail more), the new route adds a larger instance. The only reader of meta.raw is the sample_depth command.
findings.scenario: A 3:2 picture without Depth Anything downloaded: Image > Surface Maps > Compute Surface Maps, then Layer > New Light Brush Layer (or Relight), which calls ensureDepthMap -> depthFromPoints. From then on each change makes host.bundle() call ed.getValue() (autosave 1.5 s after a change), settleKey hashes getValue(), a save writes it: each call stringifies 393,216 floats twice and parses them once. Measured in plain Node on this tree: mapToJSON + JSON.stringify of a depth map whose meta.raw is a Float32Array(768*512) takes 168 ms and gives 11,005,196 bytes; autosave.json and the .scumble state grow by that per document. findings.claim: depthFromPoints stamps the new depth map with the fingerprint of the picture as it is now (meta.fp = fp), although the depth comes from the surface maps' points, which carry their own, possibly older fingerprint (points.meta.fp). A depth map made from stale points is therefore never shown as '(stale)', is reused as current by the next call, and 'Recompute' rebuilds it from the same stale points.
findings.scenario: No Depth Anything downloaded. Compute Surface Maps on picture A. Change the picture strongly (a Generate result merged in, a pasted object, a new base content at the same size, so the geometry token stays). Then Layer > New Light Brush Layer or Relight: ensureDepthMap -> computeDepthMap -> depthFromPoints builds the depth from picture A's points and stores meta.fp of the changed picture. mapStale('depth') compares meta.fp against the current picture and answers not stale; the depth row shows no '(stale)', relight shadows and depth limits follow the old scene's geometry, and Recompute (force) again reads this.maps.points without checking it. Nothing tells the user that the surface maps need recomputing.

Staleness is read from meta.fp only: lines 1101-1110 mapStale `const diff = fingerprintDiff(map.meta.fp, fp); ... return { stale: diff >= thresh, diff };`. findings.function: flushEditor (also shell.js saveBeforeRestart, host_documents.js documentDirty); root in inpaint_canvas.js syncLayersOnce
findings.claim: The fix for the upload window (f7f6e0e0, `_uploading` / `_maskUploading`) covered duplicateLayer and snapshotLayer only. findings.claim: A turn snapshot (named snapshots, the assistant's Undo this turn, and the undo/redo step of a restore) keeps the document maps by reference (`maps: { ...this.maps }`). A restore across a geometry change calls restoreGeometry -> mapExtras, which rewrites `map.xf` in place on the maps of the document being left, and those are the same objects the just-pushed 'present' snapshot holds. The incoming snapshot's maps are installed with whatever xf they were last mutated to. When the two sides hold different map objects, a map comes back with an xf of the wrong geometry.
findings.scenario: Tiles backend. Open a picture and take snapshot A (no depth map yet). Compute the depth map (M, xf = X). Crop to the right half or resize to 50 % (mapExtras sets M.xf = A·X, correct). In Undo history click Restore on A: `now = turnSnapshot()` holds M; applySnapshot(A) runs restoreGeometry with D = inv(A), and mapExtras sets M.xf = X on the object `now` holds; this.maps becomes {}. Press Ctrl+Z: applySnapshot(now) maps the empty this.maps, then installs M with xf = X in the cropped or resized document. The depth map is now shifted by the crop offset, or covers only a quarter after the resize. Every depth consumer (depth limit of filter and fill layers, lens blur, relight, select by depth, the contact shadow's fade) reads the wrong place, on screen and in exports, and getValue saves the wrong xf. A second case: snapshot A holds M1, then crop, then move the Depth map edges slider (setMapMeta makes a new object M2), then Restore A. M2 is mapped, and M1 comes back with the crop's xf in the uncropped picture. The named snapshot keeps the damaged object for later restores (copyTurn spreads `snap`).

findings.claim: newCanvas empties the document (layers, results history, saved selections, maps, guides, `this.sel = null`) before it calls setBasePixels. setBasePixels throws while Each area runs. The catch only writes a status line, so the document is left without its layers and with no selection object, although the operation was refused. The MCP command new_canvas has no guard of its own (generate_new asks host.generateNewBlocked first; new_canvas does not).
findings.scenario: Each area is running on a document (`_eachArea` is set for the whole run, eacharea.js 491-530; a local ComfyUI run sets none of the flags that the status command's `busy` reports). An MCP agent calls new_canvas {width, height} on that tab. newCanvas uploads the white canvas, then lines 398-406 clear everything, then setBasePixels throws 'Each area is running on this document: a new picture waits until it is done'. The status says the canvas could not be created, but the base is still the old picture, all layers are gone with no undo step, and `this.sel` is null. Code that dereferences it (selectionExtent, snapshotSelection in an undo, the selection overlay) throws; pushUndo returns early, so nothing is recorded any more. The autosave stores the emptied document 1.5 s later, and Each area's remaining paid areas land on it. If the requested size equals the current size, the command even returns success (commands_docs.js 243 only compares the size).
findings.evidence: inpaint_ed_histpanel.js 395-407: `const { ref } = await uploadCanvas(c, ...); const px = ...; const keep = ...; this.layers = []; this.activeLayerId = null; this.history = []; this.savedSelections = []; this.maps = {}; this.mapsVersion++; this.guides = { x: [], y: [] }; this.compare = null; this.sel = null; await this.setBasePixels(ref, px, { keepLayers: false, keep });` and 436-439 `catch (err) { ... this.setStatus("Could not create the canvas: " ...` (nothing restored). inpaint_ed_open.js 89: `if (this._eachArea) throw refusal("Each area is running on this document: a new picture waits until it is done, or stop it.");`. commands_docs.js 242 `await ed.newCanvas(`${w}x${h}`);` with no blocked check (compare commands_runs.js 42 `const blocked = host.generateNewBlocked(ed);`). inpaint_ed_history.js 446 `if (!this.sel) return;`. setBaseFromCanvas (histpanel 192-203) has the same wipe-then-throw order.
findings.fix: Refuse before anything changes: at the top of newCanvas (and again after the upload's await) check `this._eachArea`, or better host.generateNewBlocked / turnBlocked, and return with the status line. In setBaseFromCanvas do the same check before the wipe. In the new_canvas command throw host.generateNewBlocked(ed) first, as generate_new does.

findings.claim: After the mask upload's await, syncLayersOnce writes `layer.maskRef = ref` without checking that the layer still has that mask. A mask removed, applied or merged away during the upload has `maskPx = null` and `maskRef = null`. The late assignment gives the mask-less layer a mask file again; getValue writes `mask: l.maskRef` regardless of maskPx, and setValue loads it. Nothing clears it later, because the sync only looks at layers with a maskPx.
findings.scenario: A layer with an edited mask. Its mask upload is running (the 15 s autosave pass, the sync right after a document turn, or a save's flush; 50 ms to about 1 s at 15k). In that time the user clicks Remove mask, or Merge down into this layer (mergeInto sets below.maskPx = null and maskRef = null). The upload resolves and sets maskRef to the old mask's file. The autosave and any .scumble save store `mask: {old file}`. After a restart or reopen the layer has the removed mask again: a merged layer shows only where the old mask was, and an applied soft mask is applied twice. A duplicate made afterwards copies the stale maskRef too (inpaint_ed_layers.js 310).
findings.evidence: inpaint_canvas.js 915-920: `if (layer.maskDirty && layer.maskPx) { layer.maskDirty = false; layer._maskUploading = true; try { const { ref } = await uploadPixels(layer.maskPx, ...); layer.maskRef = ref;`. inpaint_ed_masks.js 15-17: `if (pixels) layer.maskDirty = !!layer.maskPx; if (!layer.maskPx) { layer.maskRef = null;`. inpaint_ed_layers.js 493: `below.maskPx = null; ... below.maskRef = null; below.maskDirty = false;`. inpaint_ed_persist.js 50 `mask: l.maskRef || null`; 262-263 and 270 setValue loads `l.mask` into maskPx.

findings.claim: A kept paint layer whose pixels and box are the size of the canvas is re-made at the new canvas size with its old pixels placed at (left, top) and its place set to 0,0. The branch checks px size and l.w / l.h but not l.x / l.y, so a full-size paint layer that was moved loses its offset: its content lands shifted by (-l.x, -l.y) against the picture. Since d6753999 hidden layers are kept too, so this now reaches ordinary hidden paint layers, not only control / reference ones.
findings.scenario: 4000 x 3000 picture. Paint on the base (addPaintLayer makes 'Paint 1' at 0,0 with W x H pixels), move it with the transform tool by (+100, +50) so x=100, y=50, w=W, h=H, px W x H. Hide it (or make it a control / reference layer). Extend the canvas by 200 px on the left. Expected: the layer's content sits at its old place plus the extension (x = 300, y = 50). Actual: px = resized(nw, nh, {x: 200, y: 0}) and l.x = l.y = 0, so the content is drawn 100 px left and 50 px up of where it was relative to the picture. No word in the status line; the hidden layer's mask (line 1657) is displaced the same way. Shown again or sent as a control image it is in the wrong place; only Ctrl+Z of the extend brings it back.
findings.fix: Take the re-size branch only when l.x === 0 && l.y === 0 (a moved layer then goes through the else branch, l.x += left; l.y += top), or place the old pixels at (left + l.x, top + l.y) and accept the cut at the new canvas edge. Add a gate step: a moved hidden full-size paint layer keeps its place against the picture after an extend.

findings.claim: Distort and warp bake the layer through a triangle mesh in which every triangle's clip is grown 0.7 px from its centroid 'so neighbouring triangles leave no seams', and each triangle draws the whole source with source-over into the new transparent canvas. In the overlap of two neighbours the same source pixel is composited twice. For opaque pixels that is harmless; for a pixel of alpha a the result is 2a - a^2 (0.5 becomes 0.75, 0.2 becomes 0.36), so every half-transparent area gets a grid of more opaque lines along all mesh edges and diagonals (24 x 24 cells for a distort, n*6 for a warp).
findings.scenario: A layer with soft alpha: a contact shadow or a soft-brush stroke at 50 %, or any cut-out with a feathered edge (a live mask is baked into the pixels first, applyPending line 184). Transform tool, Distort, drag one corner, Enter. applyPending calls drawMesh(ctx, src, dst, 24, 24): 1,152 clipped draws. Along each shared triangle edge a band of about 1 px is drawn by both triangles, so the baked layer shows a regular lattice (horizontal, vertical and diagonal lines) where alpha is up to 1.5 times what it was. The on-screen preview has the same lattice at 12 x 12. It is in the layer's pixels, so it is in every export and every run that uses the layer.
findings.fix: Draw the mesh so that overlaps cannot add up: draw each triangle into the output with globalCompositeOperation "lighter" on unexpanded, non-antialiased coverage, or keep the grown clips but composite each triangle with "destination-over" plus a final pass, or (simplest) render the mesh into a scratch per triangle and copy with "copy" inside the unexpanded triangle and "destination-over" in the grown rim, so a pixel already written is not written again. A plain-Node-free check: a 50 % grey-alpha layer distorted by the identity quad must come back with alpha 128 +- 1 everywhere.

findings.claim: With an imported tip and 'Follow stroke' on, the stamp is drawn turned, so its corners reach up to sqrt(2) x radius from the dab centre. The stroke buffer's draw box allows for that (R = rMax * 1.5 + 2), but the gesture's bounds and dirty box are padded by brushSize / 2 + 2 only. The commit (tiles and bands) and the undo copy are limited to strokeRect(p), which comes from those bounds, so whatever a turned stamp paints beyond radius + 2 px of the path's bounding box is never written to the layer.
findings.scenario: Import a square or flat rectangular tip whose bitmap is filled to its corners (a chalk or marker tip), brush size 200, Follow stroke on, paint a diagonal stroke. The stamps are turned 45 degrees and reach 141 px from the path; p.bounds is the path's box plus 102 px. At the release commitStrokeTiles clamps the written box to x0..x1 / y0..y1 of strokeRect, so the stroke's outermost stamps are cut flat along the stroke's bounding box, up to about 39 px short (0.41 r - 2). A full refresh of the view scratch during the drag (mips landing reset _strokeViewSig) shows the whole stamps, which then lose their corners at the release.
findings.fix: Pad strokeBounds and strokeDirty by the stamp's real reach when a tip is active: Math.SQRT2 * brushSize / 2 + 2 (or the R the buffer already uses, in image pixels) in layerStroke, for the flow path too.

findings.claim: Undo and redo are refused while a gesture is held (gestureHeld), but the other editing keys are not. Delete or Backspace (no selection) removes the active layer while a stroke on it is still held. The release then commits the stroke into the removed layer's pixels, which the 'Delete layer' step holds by reference (snapshotLayer keeps px by reference), and pushes a layerrect step for an id that is no longer in the document.
findings.scenario: Paint on 'Paint 1' with the button down, no selection, and hit Delete (a slip of the other hand). removeLayer pushes 'Delete layer' and drops the layer; the stroke goes on drawing into its buffer. On release commitStroke pushes 'Brush stroke' (layerrect, id of the removed layer) and writes the stroke into layer.px. Ctrl+Z #1 pops that step: applySnapshot finds no layer for it, nothing visible happens, and no redo copy is made (snapshotOf returns null for a missing layer). Ctrl+Z #2 restores the layer: it comes back with the stroke in it, because the step shared the pixels the commit wrote into. The stroke can no longer be undone on its own.

findings.claim: Select by range in mode "add" with a range that matches no pixel sets the selection's cached bounding box to the whole picture as an exact box (selectionDirty false), although the selection did not change (or is still empty). unionBounds stays null, the fallback `unionBounds || [0, 0, W, H]` is handed to boundsAfter("add", ...), which unions it with the old box and returns it as exact. getBounds() then answers [0,0,W,H] until a later replace or a rescan; every later add / marquee-add unions with it and keeps it.
findings.scenario: State: a picture with a small selection (or none); the bounds are cached exact, as they are after any selection change (markSelectionChanged -> renderInfo -> renderInfoRows calls getBounds()). Steps: Selection > Range (or MCP select_range) with mode add and a range no pixel falls in (luma lo 0.99 hi 1 on a picture without such pixels, a colour that is not in the picture with a small tol, a depth band that is empty). Every band answers bounds null. Outcome: getBounds() = [0,0,W,H]. select_range itself returns selection {x:0,y:0,w:W,h:H} to the agent; status / the info row show the whole picture as the selection's crop; with no selection at all getBounds() is non-null, so serializeForPrompt sends hasSelection true with an empty mask (inpaint_ed_persist.js 427) and comfyPlan numbers the batch's pictures as for a selection (host_provider.js 256), fillSelection / the Realism Pass 'Select an area first' guards pass; cropRect() is the whole picture (the upsampler's context picture is the whole picture at 1024 px, resolveUseCase says "outpaint" because the box touches the edges); Feather / Grow take the whole picture as their box (at 15k selectionOverTiles refuses w*h*4 > 0x7fffffff and the worker route makes a full-size bitmap); copySelection makes a W x H canvas.
findings.fix: In add mode with unionBounds null leave the bounds as they were: `hint = unionBounds ? this.boundsAfter("add", unionBounds) : this.boundsAfter("subtract", null)` (the old box as it is known: exact stays a superset that scanBoundsIn makes exact, unknown stays undefined), or pass an empty box to boundsAfter (its `empty` branch returns the old box). Add a gate step: select_range add with an empty range keeps getBounds().
findings.why: Lines are as quoted. inpaint_ed_select.js 570-577: in mode "add" the hint is `this.boundsAfter("add", unionBounds || [0, 0, W, H])`. unionBounds starts null (89) and is only set from a band's non-null bounds on every route (tiles depth 259-268, tiles luma/colour 290-299, canvas 469-479 / 545-555), so a range that matches no pixel leaves it null and the whole picture is passed. boundsAfter (inpaint_ed_export.js 501-525): b = [0,0,W,H], not empty; with the cached box known (selectionDirty false, the normal state because markSelectionChanged -> renderInfo -> renderInfoRows calls getBounds() at 590) it returns u = b when old is null, or the union with old = [0,0,W,H], as an exact box (selectionLoose false). markSelectionChanged (1516-1518) stores it with selectionDirty false, so getBounds() (527-535) never rescans and answers the whole picture although sel.combine added nothing. No guard on the way: selectRange has no early return for totalAlpha 0, oldBounds is not even read in add mode (73), and select_range (commands_select.js 199-216) and the panel (inpaint_modal.js 769) both pass mode add straight through; the command then returns bounds(ed) = the whole picture. Consequences are real: serializeForPrompt's hasSelection = !!getBounds() (inpaint_ed_persist.js 427) is true with an empty mask, the Info row shows a full-picture selection, later adds union with it. The fallback [0,0,W,H] is also used for `touched` (582), where it is harmless (a refresh area); the mistake is reusing it as the bounds hint. selectLogits handles the same case correctly. A later replace, subtract/intersect (loose -> rescan), undo or select none clears it, so a workaround exists; no pixels are lost. findings.claim: The window loop of selectLogits applies the layer clip after the intersect inversion, the pool job applies it before. With mode intersect and a source layer the loop writes the complement as `not object`, then zeroes it where the layer is transparent, so nothing is subtracted on the layer's transparent pixels: the result is sel ∩ box ∩ (object ∪ not-layer) instead of sel ∩ object ∩ layer. The worker twin was fixed for exactly this (its comment says so); the canvas twin was not, so the two backends give different selections.
findings.scenario: Canvas backend (--tiles off) or a pool that is off; in-app SAM2; Source = active layer (or an object map made of a layer); a selection that reaches over the layer's transparent area (Select all); Shift+Alt click on an object of the layer (object tool point prompt, toggleObjectAt -> host.selectPoint -> selectLogits with layer and mode intersect). Outcome: the selection keeps every pixel inside the logits' box where the layer is transparent, although those pixels are neither the object nor the layer; on tiles the same click leaves only the object's opaque pixels. A Generate or a Fill after it works on the wrong area.
findings.fix: Use the worker's rule in the loop: `const inside = v > 0 && !(clip && !clip[y * W + x]); const a = inside ? (jobInvert ? 0 : 255) : (jobInvert ? 255 : 0);`. A selection gate step on the canvas backend with a layer source and mode intersect.
findings.why:
The defect is real at a808738b, but it repeats an earlier finding that was confirmed and left open, so it is known.

**The code is as quoted.** `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js` 810-811, in the `else` branch at 786 (canvas backend or `editorPool().off`):
`let a = v > 0 ? (jobInvert ? 0 : 255) : (jobInvert ? 255 : 0); if (clip && a > 0 && !clip[y * W + x]) a = 0;`
With `mode === "intersect"`, `jobInvert` is true (735) and `bandMode` is "subtract" (736). A pixel with v <= 0 where the layer is transparent gets a = 255, is then zeroed by the clip, and so is not subtracted. After the box intersect at 732 the result is sel ∩ box ∩ (object ∪ not-layer).

**The worker twin differs.** `inpaint_worker.js` 1855-1858 computes `inside = v > 0 && !(clipBuf && !clipBuf[...])` before the inversion, and its comment names this exact failure.

**The path is reachable.** `host_helpers.js` 471 and 503 call `editor.selectLogits(res, { mode, ..., layer, ... })` with a layer (box and point prompts of the object tool). `clip = layer ? this.layerAlpha(layer) : null` at 789. I found no guard that blocks intersect with a layer on the canvas path. I did not trace `toggleObjectAt` upstream of the two `host_helpers.js` call sites.

**Already listed.** `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json` id `canvas-a/F7` (then `inpaint_canvas.js:8056`, before the file split) describes the same function, the same order of inversion and clip, the same Shift+Alt scenario and the same fix. That README lists it at line 185 as nice. It was not fixed incompletely: the window loop was never touched, the code only moved to `inpaint_ed_select.js`. `docs/BUGS.md` and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` have no entry for it (the plan's line 452 only lists the canvas backend's `logit` source as an optional kernel).

Severity nice: only the canvas backend or a pool that is off, a layer source and intersect mode, and the wrong selection is visible before a Generate or Fill.

findings.function: buildRangeBar (Pick button) / PanelsPart filter limit bar callbacks
findings.claim: The range bar's Pick calls begin() before the pick and calls neither commit nor stop when the pick answers null (Escape, or a read that gave no value). On a filter layer's limit bar begin() stores a filter snapshot in layer._undoPending, which then stays for good. The next slider or control edit of that layer finds it (`if (!layer._undoPending)`) and pushes this old snapshot as its undo step: a snapshot that also holds the filter type, name, LUT and plate of the moment of the cancelled Pick. While it stays, renderLayersUnlessEditing() returns early for the whole document.
findings.scenario: A Curves filter layer with a luma limit. Click Pick on the limit bar, press Escape ("Pick cancelled"). Change the layer's type to Levels in the type select (setFilterType pushes its own filter step and replaces filter and params; _undoPending is not looked at). Drag a Levels slider: begin keeps the stale snapshot, commit pushes it as the step. Ctrl+Z: the layer goes back to Curves with the old parameters (two steps' worth in one, the type change included), and the next Ctrl+Z applies the type step's snapshot again; redo then brings back states in the wrong order. Same with an undo between the cancelled Pick and the slider (applySnapshot's filter branch does not clear _undoPending): the slider's undo step restores the values the undo had just taken back. Meanwhile a relight nudge or wheel burst on any layer does not re-render the layer list (renderLayersUnlessEditing).
findings.fix: In the Pick handler end the edit when nothing was picked: `else if (stop) stop();`, and give the filter limit bar a cancel that drops the snapshot (`if (layer._undoPending) { this.releaseSnapshot(layer._undoPending); layer._undoPending = null; }`). Simpler: do not call begin() before the pick on the filter bar; its commit already takes the snapshot before it applies the value (panels 419-421).
findings.why:
The lines are as quoted at a808738b and no guard clears the leftover snapshot.

- **Pick handler:** renderer/editor/inpaint_rangebar.js 184-206 calls `begin()` at 186, awaits `pick()`, and commits only for a number or a "#" string. A null answer falls through with no `commit` and no `stop`.
- **Filter limit bar:** inpaint_ed_panels.js 408-410 `begin` stores `this.snapshot({kind:"filter", id})` in `layer._undoPending`. `stop` (432-435) only resets `filterPreview`. `pick` (436) is `pickOnce`, whose promise Escape resolves with null (inpaint_canvas.js 288-293, "Pick cancelled."; also inpaint_ed_pointer.js 102).
- **Nothing clears it afterwards:**
  - `cancelPreviews` / `previewShown` (inpaint_ed_depth.js 1056-1068) need `filterPreview === l.id`, which `begin` never sets.
  - `setFilterType` (inpaint_ed_filters.js 548-557) pushes its own step and replaces `filter` and `params` without touching `_undoPending`.
  - `applySnapshot`'s filter branch (inpaint_ed_history.js 816-836) does not clear it either.
  - The comment at inpaint_ed_depth.js 1051-1053 says an unshown `_undoPending` is deliberately not cancelled.
- **Consequence:** the next slider on that layer (panels 174/182, 199/208) skips taking a fresh snapshot because of `if (!layer._undoPending)` and pushes the stale one, which holds `filter`, `params`, `lut`, `plate` and `name` from the cancelled Pick. After a type change or an undo in between, Ctrl+Z restores that older state. Meanwhile `renderLayersUnlessEditing` (inpaint_ed_depth.js 1090-1092) returns early for the whole document.

Severity stays nice: with no edit between the cancelled Pick and the next slider, the stale snapshot equals the current state and is harmless. The wrong undo needs a cancelled Pick followed by a type change or undo, and only the undo history is affected, not pixels or saved data.

Not known: no match for `_undoPending`, "Pick cancelled" or the range bar in docs/BUGS.md, the three verified.json files or docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md.

findings.claim: A box description is cut to DESC_MAX (400) AFTER its @img tokens were expanded into markers, so the cut can land inside a marker. The half marker is no longer matched by LAYER_MARK (renderer) or MARKER (main) and goes to the provider as literal text in the FLUX 3 / Ideogram 4 row, and the reference is not named. Two sites: (1) the Boxes plugin's descriptions: runDesc turns '@img1' (5 chars) into '{@layer:<layer id>}' (about 20 chars), then pluginBoxes folds to 400 and only then replaces LAYER_MARK; (2) the selection's box (S1): selectionBox folds named.prompt, which already holds '{@ref:i}' markers, at 400.
findings.scenario: (1) A document with reference A (@img1) and one New box whose description is 387 characters long and ends '... wearing the hat from @img1' (valid: under DESC_MAX). Generate with FLUX 3 Image (API), Boxes switch on. descOf -> runDesc gives a 402-char string ending '{@layer:Lm3k9x2ab12}'; pluginBoxes' foldDesc slices it to 400 -> '...the hat from {@layer:Lm3k9x2ab1'; LAYER_MARK needs the closing brace, so nothing is replaced and no 'layer' refusal is thrown; main's fold/resolveMarkers leave it. findings.claim: When a PSD has no layer with pixels, both readers open its merged picture and take a fourth channel (second in grayscale) as the picture's alpha.
